resources.string: The terminal tab is the main workspace: Linux terminal, shortcut rows, and the command wheel.
Shortcut rows and Ctrl mode

The top row has `/`, `Tab`, `Esc`, and `Ctrl`; the bottom row has arrow keys.
Tap `Ctrl` to arm it and the button turns red; the next key is sent with Ctrl, and arming resets after 3 seconds without input.
Arrows move the cursor; with Ctrl armed, arrows send word-jump sequences.
The Back key acts as Esc here.
Command wheel

Swipe vertically on the shortcut bar to switch between shortcut rows and the command wheel.
Scroll horizontally, the centered card is highlighted, tap to run; a centered group expands its members above.
Tap gray area to hide the wheel; long press gray area to manage commands.
Recommendations move likely commands to the center by frequency, order, and recency.
Command library

Commands can be sorted, merged into groups, joined, or dissolved; each group keeps at least two members.\nBackup and restore are supported; restored data rejoins ranking.\nCommands support `\\n \\r \\t \\e \\cX`, with `@{}` marking the cursor landing spot.
Startup and tile commands
The startup command runs automatically when the terminal starts.\nTile startup runs the tile command.\nTile commands fit one-tap preset actions.
termlou-ui script dialogs

One shell line can open a native dialog with input, single choice, multiple choice, toggle, and colored text output.\nTheme, accent, corners, position, animation, and auto-close timeout can be adjusted.\n`termlou-clipboard` writes to the system clipboard.
Dialog and splash workshops
The dialog workshop designs dialogs visually and exports termlou-ui commands.\nThe splash workshop draws pixel art, converts photos to pixels, and adds particle boot animation.
Notes are fully local: lists manage notes, and the editor holds text, tags, and todos.
List and editor
The list shows titles, update time, and tag capsules.\nOpen a note to edit; title, body, tags, and todos stay in separate zones.
Tags
Tags are colored by content hash, so the same tag always has the same color.\nThe tags page can search and filter notes by tag.\nTap a capsule in the editor to remove a tag.
Todo board

The todo board has two columns: done on the left, open on the right, each scrolling separately with frozen titles.\nTap a whole row to toggle status, long press to delete; changes are saved immediately.
Auto save

Text is compared and saved when leaving the editor.\nLeaving the list, switching notes or tabs, backgrounding, and opening subpages all trigger it.\nNo manual save is needed, and there is no per-keystroke write amplification.
Tile shortcut
The tile can open the standalone notes page directly.\nIt never wakes the terminal or Linux session.\nExit returns to the launcher with no background residue.
The files tab manages `/workspace`: navigation, import, sharing, and deletion.
Navigation and info
Enter folders, go up, see folder marks and file sizes.\nThe list has a fade-in animation.
Import
Bottom buttons import files in any format.\nWhole folders can be imported recursively.
Share and export
Files are shared directly.\nFolders are packed as ZIP before sharing.
Delete
Files are deleted directly.\nNon-empty folders ask for confirmation first.
Type recognition
Common types are recognized by extension.\nText, images, archives, code, and documents are separated automatically.
The network tab captures per-app traffic and analyzes flows: choose apps first, then read logs, rankings, and blocks.
Per-app capture
Select target apps through VPN.\nDNS follows the system; public DNS is only a fallback.
Flow log
The live list shows domain or IP, protocol, port, up and down bytes, and status.\nBlocking by IP or domain is supported.
Rankings and DNS
Traffic rankings are grouped by domain or port.\nDNS history maps queries to responses.
Proxy and blocking
Built-in SOCKS5 with optional upstream proxy; block rules take effect immediately.\nOnly plaintext is parsed, with no TLS interception.
Settings holds all switches and commands; language and theme changes need a restart.
Display
Five terminal font sizes sync immediately.\nLanguage and theme switch between Chinese and English or dark and light, then need a restart.
Commands
The startup command runs when the terminal starts.\nThe tile command is for one-tap tile actions.\nQuick launch chooses frequently used apps.
Workshops
The dialog workshop designs script dialogs and exports commands.\nThe splash workshop customizes the boot screen.
Network and keep-alive
Empty upstream proxy means built-in direct mode.\nLAN shares files and the terminal.\nKeep-alive uses a low-priority foreground service.
